name: nvidia-driver
summary: The NVIDIA driver branch (and the open kernel modules or not)
description: Installs the driver branch (Ubuntu's server packages, NVIDIA's CUDA repository, DNF module streams, SUSE's G06 packages) and loads it. A different driver already loaded is swapped only while no process holds the GPUs; otherwise the unit reports `RebootRequired`. It keeps `nvidia-persistenced` running where it is installed.

name: container-toolkit
summary: The NVIDIA container toolkit, generating CDI specs
description: Installs the NVIDIA container toolkit, configures containerd and Docker with its runtime (with `cdi`, CDI enabled), and regenerates `/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml` whenever the driver or the GPU and MIG device list changes. With `cdi` (the default), a container gets GPUs only by the CDI names bcd hands out. The unit sets `accept-nvidia-visible-devices-envvar-when-unprivileged` and `accept-nvidia-visible-devices-as-volume-mounts` to false in `/etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml`. Otherwise an unprivileged container could choose GPUs other tenants hold with `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (the packaged config leaves that key at its permissive default). On a Kubernetes node that is the `ForeignGpuExposure` condition.

name: mig-layout
summary: A MIG layout: a named profile per GPU, or the pool's layout
description: Partitions every MIG-capable GPU to the layout: `all-disabled`, `all-<profile>` (as many as fit, e.g. `all-1g.10gb`) or `mixed:<n>x<profile>+<profile>…` (per GPU, e.g. `mixed:3g.40gb+2x2g.20gb`), with a compute instance in each GPU instance. A GPU holding allocations or running compute processes is left as it is until they end (under `bcd helper`, the helper sees that itself, never taking the node's word). A MIG mode change that needs a GPU reset, which fails, reports `RebootRequired`.

name: fabric-manager
summary: NVIDIA Fabric Manager for NVSwitch systems
description: On NVSwitch systems only (nothing to do elsewhere): installs and runs NVIDIA Fabric Manager; node condition `FabricManagerDown`, which makes the node NoSchedule, while it is not running.

name: sysctl
description: Free-form: each key a sysctl name with a scalar value, written to `/etc/sysctl.d/90-bcd.conf` and set live. A key the kernel does not have yet (its module is not loaded) is retried. Keys that would run programs as root or lower the host's defenses are refused (`kernel.core_pattern`, `kernel.modprobe`, `kernel.usermodehelper.*`, `fs.binfmt_misc.*`, `kernel.randomize_va_space`, `kernel.yama.*`, `user.*` and the like), and a few take only their hardened values: `dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti` and `dev.tty.ldisc_autoload` only 0, `kernel.io_uring_disabled` only 1 or 2, `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start` only 1024 and above.

name: hugepages
summary: Huge pages: 2 MiB pages allocated at runtime, 1 GiB pages through the kernel command line (effective after a reboot), and the transparent huge page policy
description: 2 MiB pages are allocated at runtime; 1 GiB pages at runtime when the kernel finds the memory, else through the boot loader (`hugepagesz=1G hugepages=N`) with `RebootRequired`. With `perNuma` the counts are per NUMA node. 1 GiB pages are mounted at `/dev/hugepages1G` (a systemd mount unit), 2 MiB pages at systemd's `/dev/hugepages`.

name: gpu-sharing
summary: How a shared pool's GPUs are split between clients: MPS (bcd-mps.service, 100/replicas % of the SMs each) or time-slicing (MPS stopped)
description: `mps` runs the MPS control daemon (`bcd-mps.service`, each client limited to 100/`replicas` percent of the SMs, node condition `MPSDown` while it is down); `timeslice` stops it.

name: cpu
summary: Host CPUs: the cpufreq governor (live), and CPUs isolated from the kernel scheduler for pinned VMs and holds (isolcpus/nohz_full/rcu_nocbs, effective after a reboot)
description: Sets the frequency governor on every CPU that has one, and isolates CPUs from the scheduler for pinned vCPUs (`isolcpus`, `nohz_full`, `rcu_nocbs` through the boot loader, `RebootRequired` until the kernel shows them isolated). CPU 0 is never isolated.

name: iommu
summary: The IOMMU for GPU passthrough to VMs and sandboxes: intel_iommu=on or amd_iommu=on (by CPU vendor) and iommu=pt on the kernel command line, effective after a reboot
description: Turns the IOMMU on for GPUs passed through to VMs and sandboxes (`intel_iommu=on` or `amd_iommu=on`, and `iommu=pt` unless `passthrough` is false) through the boot loader, with `RebootRequired` until an IOMMU is active.

name: gpu-settings
summary: Per-GPU settings kept by bcd: the power cap (nvidia-smi -pl, re-applied on drift) and ECC (effective after a reboot)
description: Caps each GPU's board power (applied again whenever it drifts; outside a GPU's range the unit fails) and sets the ECC mode, which changes at the GPU's next reset (`RebootRequired` until then).

name: kernel-modules
summary: Kernel modules loaded at boot and now (modules-load.d), with their options (modprobe.d): kvm_intel/kvm_amd, vhost_net and tun for VM hosts
description: Modules loaded now and at every boot (`/etc/modules-load.d/bcd.conf`) with their options (`/etc/modprobe.d/bcd.conf`). A loaded module whose options differ is reloaded only when nothing uses it; otherwise they apply when it next loads. Sandbox hosts load `kvm_intel` or `kvm_amd`, `vhost_net`, `tun` and, for GPU passthrough, `vfio-pci`. Options that turn off DMA isolation for passed-through devices (`vfio` `enable_unsafe_noiommu_mode`, `vfio_iommu_type1` `allow_unsafe_interrupts`) are refused.

name: k8s-join
summary: Joins the node to a Kubernetes cluster as a worker (kubeadm join with a bootstrap token fetched by reference) and keeps its kubelet, labels and taints; GPUs through containerd's NVIDIA runtime and CDI
description: Joins the machine to a Kubernetes cluster as a worker with a bootstrap token fetched through the secret broker, only to clusters root pins in `[kubernetes] allowed_clusters` under `bcd helper`. See [Kubernetes](/docs/daemon/kubernetes).
